material_definitions: The substitution of P5+ with Si4+ was performed in the solid solutions Li(6+x)P(1-x)Si(x)S5X to study aliovalent doping effects in Li+ conducting argyrodites.
Structural characterizations (X-ray and neutron diffraction) combined with electrochemical impedance spectroscopy were used to evaluate the effect of increasing Si4+ content on ionic conductivity.
The Si4+ doping increases the unit cell size, the Li+ concentration, and the occupancy of Li+ on the transition state for hopping.
Aliovalent Si4+ doping leads to an optimized conductivity greater than 2 mS cm-1.
The study investigates the ionic transport properties of Li(6+x)P(1-x)Si(x)S5Br solid solutions by varying the Si4+ content (x).
Temperature-dependent impedance spectroscopy was performed on all samples.
All impedance data were fit using an equivalent circuit consisting of one parallel CPE/resistor in series with a CPE.
The increasing Si4+ content leads to increased Li+ concentration and corresponding higher bulk conductivity, with the materials categorized as argyrodite superionics.
